issues.body: The held branch emits an ALERT and correction whenever `age_unpark_state` finds a grant matching the newest groom age-park receipt. That only proves a historical grant exists; it does not prove the currently live `review:parked` label is the label that grant attempted to remove. The same function's convergence branch explicitly compares the grant timestamp with `park_applications` because `review:parked` is shared by multiple writers. The held branch skips that check. Reachable sequence: groom age-parks, groom grants and successfully removes the label, another writer later applies `review:parked`, and a human hold is live. The new branch then says the earlier re-admission is withdrawn and asks a human to remove the current park, even though the earlier re-admission completed and the current label represents a distinct later decision. This is misleading trust-plane evidence and can direct a human to undo a valid park.
issues.fix_hint: Before classifying the state as a stall, prove that the grant is strictly newer than every relevant park application, using the same fail-closed timestamp/readability discipline as the convergence branch (without authorizing any label write). If a later or unreadable park application exists, do not post the correction. Add a held-path test with a matching old grant plus a newer shared-writer park event and assert no ALERT/comment and a zero stall gauge.
issues.title: Stall correction mistakes a later shared-writer park for the old grant's residue

issues.body: `_execute_age_unpark_actions` now returns four values `(outcome, grants, convergences, stalls)`, and its caller unpacks four, but its annotation remains `tuple[PhaseOutcome, int, int]`. The public contract and implementation disagree, which will mislead readers and static checking.
issues.fix_hint: Change the annotation to `tuple[PhaseOutcome, int, int, int]`.
issues.title: Return annotation still declares three values

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The DELETE post-state verification is fail-closed and the added tests exercise both response and read-back paths. However, the new held-stall path treats any matching historical age-unpark grant as evidence about the currently live shared park label. It omits the recency/ownership distinction that the convergence path already requires, so a later park by another writer is falsely reported as a failed or withdrawn re-admission. That makes the correction unsound and requires changes.
